findings.issue: Handoff review: the bound repository digest followed the caller's spelling of the path. fs.realpathSync keeps the drive-letter and casing spelling on Windows, and a child inherits its parent's spelling of the working directory. Measured on this workstation: c:\Users\... and C:\Users\... gave different root digests for one directory, so after adoption one process would read the policy as unverifiable and refuse all new work
findings.resolution: One helper, constitutionPhysicalRoot (fs.realpathSync.native), used by the reader, the run binding and the owner writer. New scenario over three other spellings of one adopted TEMP repository (read, bind, append). Windows-only negative control restores the old call and is caught. Failed closed before the fix; no rule was weakened

findings.issue: Handoff review: the adoption directory, the writer lock directory and the bootstrap staging directory had no .gitignore rule, unlike every sibling data/brain runtime subtree. Adoption would have made the repository look dirty to the observer, the cleanliness gates and the eval baseline overlay check
findings.resolution: Three anchored .gitignore rules, confirmed with git check-ignore. New scenario asserts the rules and that they name everything the writer creates. Negative control removes the rule and is caught
